problem.problem:
Bob is rough. Charlie is nice. Charlie is rough. Charlie is white. Dave is not white. Gary is cold. Gary is quiet. Rough, white things are quiet. If Charlie is round and Charlie is quiet then Charlie is rough. All young things are round. Nice things are white. Rough, nice things are cold. If something is round and rough then it is nice. If something is rough then it is young.

Determine whether the following statement is true, false, or unknown:
Charlie is quiet.
raw_logic_programs:
Predicates:
Rough($x, bool) ::: Is x rough?
Nice($x, bool) ::: Is x nice?
White($x, bool) ::: Is x white?
NotWhite($x, bool) ::: Is x not white?
Cold($x, bool) ::: Is x cold?
Quiet($x, bool) ::: Is x quiet?
Round($x, bool) ::: Is x round?
Young($x, bool) ::: Is x young?

Facts:
Rough(Bob, True) ::: Bob is rough.
Nice(Charlie, True) ::: Charlie is nice.
Rough(Charlie, True) ::: Charlie is rough.
White(Charlie, True) ::: Charlie is white.
NotWhite(Dave, True) ::: Dave is not white.
Cold(Gary, True) ::: Gary is cold.
Quiet(Gary, True) ::: Gary is quiet.

Rules:
Rough($x, True) && White($x, True) >>> Quiet($x, True) ::: Rough, white things are quiet.
Round(Charlie, True) && Quiet(Charlie, True) >>> Rough(Charlie, True) ::: If Charlie is round and Charlie is quiet then Charlie is rough.
Young($x, True) >>> Round($x, True) ::: All young things are round.
Nice($x, True) >>> White($x, True) ::: Nice things are white.
Rough($x, True) && Nice($x, True) >>> Cold($x, True) ::: Rough, nice things are cold.
Round($x, True) && Rough($x, True) >>> Nice($x, True) ::: If something is round and rough then it is nice.
Rough($x, True) >>> Young($x, True) ::: If something is rough then it is young.

Query:
Quiet(Charlie, True) ::: Charlie is quiet.
